title: The task set, the timer set, their codes and their values, and the element set of the route-start answer are not published
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-012 Data table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.12.1 to A2.12.3.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T3.1, T3.2, T-A.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-RES-01, R-SET-01, R-DIL-01, R-LIT-01); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (FEAT-VAL-12); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 5 and 8; s8 BR1, BR2; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.8; s13 Configuration; s14; CON s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 4; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.8; s14
description: Both legacy criteria say the chosen route is opened, its tasks created and its clocks started, and both stories therefore need the task set and the timer set of each route with their codes and values. The legacy Data table names the task and timer entities with DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-036 and no code and no value; the FSD A2.12 states the act and names no task code, timer type or duration; TSD S1 T3.1 defines valuation and score only and T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE; the routing logic carries a timer column with row-level values such as 2 working days and same day, and no governed row identifier for a route set. TSD S1 T-A.2 gives the request and answer type names with no field table, so the element set of the route-start answer is not published either. The stories therefore read the sets as governed rows with their version, record that version, assert no code, no duration and no default, and the contract declares the elements with their source and no value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-012 AC1 'opens the chosen route, creates its tasks and starts its clocks' with the Data rows task (DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026) and timer (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); FSD S1 A2.12.3.1 gives VR-S1-012-1 and BR-S1-012 only; TSD S1 T3.1 lists valuation and score, T3.2 lists LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE, T-A.2 gives Request 'RouteRequest' and Response 'Approval' with no field list; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-01, R-SET-01, R-DIL-01 and R-LIT-01 give actions, to states and timer values with no set identifier.
area: Reference data and API contract, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: Owner of the route sets in rwb-decision with the business owner of module S1 and the owner of the task and timer reference data
proposed: The route-set owner publishes the task set and the timer set of each route as governed rows with a version, and the contract author publishes the route-start element set with their types and nullability; the step then reads the sets with their version and records it, and the contract declares the elements with their source and no value.

title: The four consumed rows publish no operation name, the plan carries no class C row, and no source says which service owns the task and timer rows after the split
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3, T5.1, T5.2, T-A.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.12.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-012 Data table); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.4, R5.5)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2, 3, 8; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; CON s12.2, s12.7, s12.8
description: The step reads the case state and answers the route start to rwb-case, reads the rule row in force and the governed task and timer sets from rwb-decision, and authorises through rwb-access, and no source publishes an operation name, a parameter or a transport for any of those rows. The ownership rows of the context pack name three provided S1 operations, no table, no event, no job and one workflow, and name no consumed operation. TSD S1 T-A.1 lists only API-S1-001 and T5.1 is the row 'None'; T5.2 names published Java interfaces of P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation. The legacy Data table lists task and timer as entities of the feature and TSD S1 T3.1 gives them no home in S1, so the split assigns them to rwb-case by the ownership rows and the stories write neither row. The plan rows for both slices carry C as an empty list, so the four rows are built against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the contract row carries the placeholder.
evidence: Context pack S1 ownership rows: three REST operations, zero tables, zero events, zero jobs, one workflow; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; TSD S1 T5.2 names published Java interfaces with no operation; FSD S1 A2.12.2 states the integration points as 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler'; the legacy Data table lists task and timer with DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-036 and TSD S1 T3.1 defines neither; split_plan.json carries C as an empty list for both slices.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The three owners publish their operation names before the wave 3 tag, and rwb-case confirms that it creates the task and timer rows from the answered sets; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use in the meantime, and a published name is a minor version of the baseline.

title: No S1 rule package is in force and no source names the rule id, the rule row or the parameter of the route-start step
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.12.3.1 BR-S1-012, A2.12.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2, T8); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (Rules sheet); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-12)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s8 BR1, BR6; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1; s14
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and no S1 route-start rule id is in force for this feature: the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries the route sets R-RES, R-SET, R-DIL and R-LIT with a row per approved route and no S1 package row for the step, the S1 package is Phase 2 in the detailed design, and TSD S1 T8 maps every requirement to FEAT-VAL-01. No source names the parameter, the reference-data row or the owner of the task and timer sets either. The story writes whatever rule id and version the rwb-decision answer carries into the decision record and never writes a route, a to state, a task code or a duration in code.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.12.3.1 gives VR-S1-012-1 and BR-S1-012 and A2.12.4.1 states the result is recorded with its rule version; the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-RES-01, R-SET-01, R-DIL-01 and R-LIT-01 with no S1 package row for the start; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE only; TSD S1 T8 maps the requirements to FEAT-VAL-01 and gives no rule id.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule owner names the route-start rule of each route set and its reference-data rows and publishes the S1 package, or confirms that the route rows stay governed rows of rwb-decision; the record then carries that id and version with no change to the behaviour.
